item.title: A combined PRIMER+MINERVA study of the evolution of $\mathbf{[O\mbox{III}]+H\beta}$ equivalent width from $\mathbf{z=3}$ to $\mathbf{z=8.5}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analysis of the evolution of $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent width ($W_{\lambda}$) over the redshift range $z=3$ to $z=8.5$, based on combining the JWST NIRCam PRIMER and MINERVA imaging in the UDS survey field. We find that the combined medium- and broad-band data set reduces the photometric redshift outlier rate to $\eta = 4.7\%$ at $m_{\rm F444W}\leq28$, a $42\%$ reduction compared with PRIMER imaging alone. We also demonstrate that the combined data set facilitates the accurate recovery of $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent widths in redshift bins centred on $z\sim3.2,\, 4.0,\, 5.0,\, 7.2,\, 8.3$; corresponding to the F210M, F250M, F300M, F410M and F460M filters. Based on a final sample of $N=1964$ galaxies with $M_{\rm UV}\leq-19.25$, we first provide new constraints on the bright end of the $z=7-8$ $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ luminosity function ($\log_{10}\phi^{*} = -4.3_{-0.5}^{+0.2}$, $\log_{10}L^{*} = -43.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}$), before proceeding to investigate the redshift evolution of $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent width. Using SED modelling based on non-parametric continuity star-formation histories, we find that the median $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent width monotonically increases with redshift, rising from $\mathrm{log}_{10}(W_{\lambda})=2.54^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$ at $z\simeq 3$ to $\mathrm{log}_{10}(W_{\lambda})=3.05^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$ at $z\simeq 8$. In tandem, the distribution of $\mathrm{log}_{10}(W_{\lambda})$ is observed to become increasingly asymmetric with redshift, producing a fraction of extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs, $W_{\lambda}>1000\,$\r{A}) that reaches $f_{\rm EELG}=0.50\pm{0.10}$ by $z=8.3$. Our SED modelling results indicate that the physical driver of this evolution is increasingly bursty star-formation, with EELGs the result of particularly high specific star-formation rates over the 10 Myr prior to observation.

item.title: Constraining Dust Attenuation Curves in Star-Forming Galaxies at Cosmic Noon Using Multiple Emission Line Ratios
item.description: arXiv:2611.08594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dust attenuation remains a dominant systematic uncertainty in measurements of an emission line, and therefore galaxies properties derived from the emission lines such as star formation rates. Corrections based only on the Balmer decrement require an assumed attenuation-curve slope, even though that slope varies among galaxies. We use JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from JADES to constrain effective dust attenuation curves for 386 star-forming galaxies at $0.5\leq z\leq7$. For each galaxy, we combine H$\alpha$, H$\beta$, and one additional hydrogen recombination line and solve for the normalization $\tau_V$ and slope $n$ of a power-law attenuation curve, allowing the slope to vary from galaxy to galaxy. We found slopes and normalization span a broad range even for galaxies at similar redshifts. Additionally, our method using Paschen transitions provided substantially greater constraints the attenuation-curve slope than Balmer-only combinations. When comparing to SMC-like or Calzetti-like corrections we find our method produces more consistent star formation rates with less scatter. These improved dust corrections provide an avenue to better describe star formation rates in the epoch of peak star formation and the early universe.

item.title: FORGE'd In The Early Universe II: Constraining The Pop III Initial Mass Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.08598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a cosmological radiation-magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) zoom-in simulation of $56$ Population III stars using FORGE'd in FIRE. Our simulation combines a cosmological initial condition centered on an isolated ultra-faint galaxy ($M_{\mathrm{halo}} \sim 10^9 M_\odot$ at $z=0$) with individual-star formation and feedback physics, reaching a maximum mass resolution of $\sim 10^{-2} M_\odot$ and spatial resolution of $\sim 10^{-3} \mathrm{pc}$. We follow continued star formation for just over $500$ Myr, from $z \sim 16$ to $z \sim 7$, substantially longer than what has been achieved before, and track star formation across five distinct minihalos. From our stellar population, we self-consistently resolve an emergent stellar initial mass function (IMF) and find $\alpha = 1.9$ for $dN/dM \propto M^{-\alpha}$ at $M_{\star} \gtrsim 2.2 M_{\odot}$. Additionally, we form both single and multiple stellar systems, including binaries and higher-order multiples, as well as stars with masses below $1 M_{\odot}$. At early times, the stellar mass distribution is more top-heavy, with a high-mass slope of $\alpha\sim1.4-1.5$, similar to previous Pop. III simulations, and steepens as star formation continues. This suggests that differences between our final IMF and previous studies may partly reflect the much longer evolution followed here, approximately five orders of magnitude longer than in several previous Pop. III sink-particle simulations. The first star-forming minihalo, which hosts the most massive stars in our simulation, has a shallower IMF slope of $\alpha\approx 1$, while later-forming minihalos produce lower maximum stellar masses in lower-density parent clouds.

item.title: Magnetically Arrested Accretion and Black Hole Spin in a Semi-Analytic Model of Galaxy Formation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present {\sc Mad Sage}, a semi-analytic model of galaxy formation that couples black hole mass and spin evolution to gas accretion and AGN feedback under magnetically arrested disk conditions. Building on the {\sc Dark Sage} model, we incorporate GRMHD-calibrated prescriptions for spin evolution and jet power, spin-dependent radiative efficiencies, and remnant spins from BH-BH mergers. We compare accretion and feedback models, including coherent disk-fed accretion with mixed coherent and incoherent hot-halo accretion, with and without additional mechanical feedback. We find that incoherent accretion, together with Blandford-Znajek spin-down, drives massive BHs toward low spins, reducing jet efficiencies and weakening the quenching of massive galaxies. Reproducing the high-mass end of the stellar mass function requires either exclusively coherent accretion or an additional feedback component provided by ADAF outflows. Our models broadly reproduce observed BH-galaxy scaling relations, disk surface density profiles, and the AGN luminosity function at $z\sim 2-6$, although the spin models under-predict the number density of faint AGN at low redshift. At $z\lesssim 3$, predicted BH spins decrease with increasing BH mass, while at higher redshifts, the mass dependence weakens. Spin distributions peak at $|a_\star|\sim 0.5$-$0.7$, below current X-ray reflection spectroscopy measurements, and become bimodal for massive, quiescent BHs accessible with the next generation Event Horizon Telescope and the Black Hole EXplorer. We report that the predicted LISA event rates are nearly independent of the adopted accretion and spin models.

item.title: FORGE'd in Fragments: Pop III star formation in a Milky Way-like progenitor halo
item.description: arXiv:2611.08603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a radiation-magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) cosmological zoom-in simulation of Pop III star formation, drawing initial conditions from a Milky Way-like progenitor halo at redshift $z \sim 21$. We follow the collapse of primordial gas over 10 orders of magnitude, through to the formation of an accretion disk that becomes gravitationally unstable $\Delta t \sim -3$ kyr before the first protostar's formation. Prominent spiral arms then develop and fragment vigorously, producing $\sim 60$ sink formation events over the first $8$ kyr post-collapse evolution, with a total stellar mass reaching $> 150\,{\rm M_\odot}$ by $15$ kyr, the end of our simulation. The disk remains magnetically supercritical throughout: the mass-to-flux ratio falls from $\mu_\Phi \sim 10^2$-$10^3$ to $\sim 15$ by $15$ kyr, as the inflow brings in magnetic flux. The magnetic energy in the disk remains sub-dominant throughout, but grows by $\sim 3.5$ orders of magnitude after the first star forms. The disk starts sub-virial and reaches virial equilibrium within $\sim 2$ kyr. The total stellar mass of the population grows as $M_* \propto t^2$, confirming the prediction of accelerating accretion in self-gravitating turbulent collapse, at rates of $\dot{M} \sim 10^{-3}$-$10^{-2}\,{\rm M}_\odot {\rm yr}^{-1}$. The star formation efficiency reaches $\approx 90\%$ within the disk (after $\approx 11$ kyr; $\approx 80\%$ at $9.5$ kyr) and $\sim 50\%$ within a $0.1$ pc sphere. We find a top heavy IMF ($dN/dm \propto m^{-\alpha}$) with a high-mass slope $\alpha \approx 1$. The cosmological environment sets the boundary conditions of the disk: an envelope delivers $\sim 3\times 10^{-3}\,{\rm M}_\odot {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to the outer edge of a disk with a radius of $\sim 10^{3}$ AU; the disk spreads and, in our simulation, its fragmentation sites move outward, from $\sim 500$ to $\sim 1350$\,AU, until it has been depleted.

item.title: Jeans Dynamical Constraints on the IMF in Massive Quiescent Galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ from JWST/NIRSpec
item.description: arXiv:2611.08612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present dynamical masses for nine massive quiescent galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ from the JWST-IMFERNO program, measured from ultra-deep ($\sim32$hr), spatially resolved NIRSpec/MSA spectroscopy combined with NIRCam imaging. The most massive of these galaxies have previously been found to have a bottom-heavy initial mass function (IMF), based on measurements of dwarf-sensitive absorption features. Here, we examine whether the stellar masses inferred for these IMFs are consistent with the dynamical masses of these galaxies. We derive the dynamical masses by including Jeans Anisotropic Modelling within a forward-modelling framework that accounts for instrumental optics, source morphology, and geometric effects. We compare the resulting dynamical masses to the stellar masses for different IMF assumptions. A Milky Way IMF produces physically plausible dynamical-to-stellar mass ratios but implies central dark matter fractions ($f_{\rm DM,1R_e}=0.54\pm0.06$) that are a factor $\sim2$ higher compared to local ETGs and simulations. When uniformly applying the IMF that was measured from absorption features, the mean dark matter fraction becomes low ($f_{\rm DM,1R_e}=0.02\pm0.18$), and the stellar masses exceed the dynamical mass at $2\sigma$ significance for two out of seven galaxies in the sample. When we adopt the measured IMF only in the central $R_e$ and use a MW IMF in the outskirts, we find realistic dark matter fractions ($f_{\rm DM,1R_e}=0.28\pm0.12$) and consistent dynamical masses. These results support a scenario where the cores of the most massive quiescent galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ had a bottom-heavy IMF, similar to those observed in the centres of local early-type galaxies. Our results are consistent with an inside-out growth scenario, in which size and mass growth of massive galaxies proceeds after quenching through minor mergers, leaving the bottom-heavy cores mostly intact.

item.title: Digging into the Interior of Hot Cores with ALMA (DIHCA). VIII. Feeding a high-mass binary system in the making
item.description: arXiv:2611.08641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the gas kinematics in the proto-binary NGC 6334I(N) ALMAe9-ALMAe14 system with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 1.33 mm with an angular resolution of 66 mas (~90 au). With a separation of 740 au between the system members, these observations allow a detailed study of the gas motion around this likely binary system hosting at least one growing high-mass star. Some CH$_3$OH lines tracing cold gas ($E_u/k_B$~100 K) reveal the presence of ordered circumbinary gas motion around the binary system within a ~1000 au radius, and rotation around the individual sources with rotation axes pointing roughly in the same direction. We estimate a central source mass, uncorrected for inclination, of 2 M$_\odot$ for the secondary, while the primary has an estimated mass of 5 M$_\odot$ as reported in previous works. The CH$_3$OH transitions with higher $E_u/k_B$ ($\gtrsim400$ K) values reveal circumstellar gas rotation in ALMAe9 consistent with the cold gas tracers. The vibrationally excited SO emission also traces rotation around ALMAe9 and potentially an accretion shock from a flow feeding the circumstellar disk of ALMAe14. We identify two potential inflows feeding the circumstellar disks from the circumbinary gas at rates of ~$10^{-6}-10^{-4}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ from CH$_3$OH emission. An additional third inflow seems to be feeding the primary from gas at larger scales.

item.title: TRGB Distances to the Andromeda Dwarf Satellites from the INT Monitoring Survey
item.description: arXiv:2611.08648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We measure tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) distances to 17 dwarf satellites of M31 from Sloan $i$-band photometry of the Isaac Newton Telescope (INT) monitoring survey of Local Group dwarf galaxies, and add the distances of And I, And VII and And IX from earlier papers of the survey. We locate the tip with a Sobel edge-detection filter applied to the luminosity function of stars within two half-light radii of each galaxy. The distance moduli range from $23.38 \pm 0.06$ mag (And XVI, 474 kpc) to $25.35 \pm 0.06$ mag (And XVIII, 1177 kpc), and 15 of the 20 satellites lie between 650 and 850 kpc. For most galaxies, our distance agrees with at least one published value. Compared with Conn et al. (2012), our tip is brighter for 12 of the 18 galaxies in common, by up to 0.39 mag, possibly because of crowding in the central regions. And XII lies at $844^{+40}_{-38}$ kpc, about 60 kpc behind M31, consistent with a first infall into the Local Group. And XXII lies at $753^{+28}_{-27}$ kpc, closer than all earlier estimates, and about 59 kpc from M33 in three dimensions (for an M33 distance of 794 kpc), consistent with an association with M33. And XVIII lies about 400 kpc behind M31, too far for a secure association with M31.
item.dc:creator: Hedieh Abdollahi

item.title: KCWI Observations of Type 2 Quasar-driven Ionized Outflows at z~0.1
item.description: arXiv:2611.08828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AGN-driven outflows play a crucial role in regulating star formation in galaxies. These outflows are known to be multi-phase, and the characterization of the kinematics, extent, and energetics of each gas phase is needed to obtain a full picture of the outflow properties and impact. This study presents Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) integral field spectroscopy of the ionized gas outflow properties in seven low redshift (z<0.1) quasars---six Type 2 AGN and one narrow-line Type 1 AGN---providing insight into the warm ionized outflows in these luminous AGN. With the large field-of-view and high sensitivity of KCWI, these data reveal both larger ionized outflow extents than were previously known for these sources and uncover the existence of additional high-velocity kinematic components in the ionized outflows of these luminous AGN. We find (a) a high incidence (50-70%) of multiple outflows on scales of 4--10 kpc and (b) trends between the outflow extent, kinematics, and the ionized mass and energy outflow rates. These trends imply that the faster and often smaller outflows carry higher mass and energy outflow rates than the slower, larger outflows. We also find that the ionized gas outflows reach as far as the known extent of narrow-line ionized gas emission in AGN, which is known to depend weakly on AGN luminosity. This work highlights the utility of the current generation of wide-field integral field spectrographs on 8--10m class telescopes for studying quasar-driven outflows.

item.title: Predicting Continuum Emission in Massive Star-Forming Regions with Embedded HII Regions - Dust, Free-Free, and Anomalous Microwave Emission with POLARIS
item.description: arXiv:2611.08891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Context: HII regions are a key stage of massive star formation, where ionizing radiation reshapes the interstellar medium. Their continuum spectra trace thermal dust, free-free emission, and anomalous microwave emission (AME). Aims: We investigate how these components evolve as an HII region expands and correlate with gas and electron column densities across spatial scales. Methods: We post-process RAMSES radiation-magnetohydrodynamical simulations of a $10^4 M_\odot$ cloud with POLARIS. The model includes grain charging, rotational excitation and damping, radiative torques, rotational disruption, and emission from dust, ionized gas, and nano-composite grains. We compute maps and SEDs for six snapshots over $1-10^4$ GHz and analyze multi-scale correlations. Results: Ionized emission evolves from a compact, optically thick HII region to an extended, optically thin structure. Around 15 GHz, free-free emission changes from a $\nu^2$ to a $\nu^{-0.1}$ spectral regime as optical depth decreases, and increasingly traces electron column density. The thermal dust peak shifts from mid- to far-infrared as colder material contributes, while dust emission remains strongly correlated with total gas column density. AME peaks at 26-37 GHz and shows scale-dependent correlations with gas and electron distributions. Rotational disruption is the main dust-destruction mechanism affecting mid-infrared emission and the high-frequency AME tail. Conclusions: These continuum components provide complementary, scale-dependent diagnostics of stellar feedback. Self-consistent multi-frequency modeling is essential for interpreting surveys of star-forming clouds.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Reissl, Alessio Traficante, Paolo Suin, Alice Nucara, Ralf S. Klessen, Leonardo Testi

item.title: Identifying Chemically Coherent Stellar Families in the Galactic High-{\alpha} Disk with Low-Resolution Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.08983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identification of chemical substructures in the Galactic high-{\alpha} disk provides valuable insight into its formation history. In this work, we demonstrate the capability of low-resolution spectroscopy for this purpose by applying DBSCAN clustering to 87,275 red giants in the high-{\alpha} disk using 18 elemental abundances derived from LAMOST low-resolution spectra (R~1800). We assess the effectiveness of this approach by comparing the clustering results from the low-resolution data with those obtained by applying the same procedure to high-resolution survey abundances and to mock catalogs. These comparisons suggest that, despite the relatively large uncertainties in individual elemental abundances derived from low-resolution spectra, the astrophysical coherence among different elements provides sufficient information to identify chemically coherent families that may share similar enrichment histories without necessarily sharing a common birth environment. After scanning the parameter space of the DBSCAN procedure and merging the results from different parameter combinations, we identify 133 candidate chemical families containing 4,642 unique stars (5.3% of the high-{\alpha} disk sample). These families exhibit diverse multi-element abundance patterns, with particularly prominent differences in neutron-capture elements at nearly identical [Fe/H] values. These families therefore offer new constraints on the diversity of chemical enrichment pathways and on the assembly history of the high-{\alpha} disk.
item.dc:creator: Tianmin Wu, Maosheng Xiang, Jianrong Shi, Tiancheng Sun, Meng Zhang

item.title: Phosphorus-rich star formation in giant molecular clouds hosting primordial globular clusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.09044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent observational studies have identified phosphorus-rich (P-rich) stars ([P/Fe]>1.0) in both Galactic globular clusters (GCs) including three confirmed cases and the field population. Using analytical models of GC formation, we investigate a scenario in which P-rich stars form from pristine gas in GC-forming giant molecular clouds (GMCs) polluted by oxygen-neon (ONe) novae within and surrounding the GMCs. Within this framework, we model the chemical abundance patterns of P-rich stars using diverse chemical yield sets for ONe novae while varying the dilution factor (Fdil), defined as the ratio of pristine gas mass to total ONe nova ejecta mass. The principal results of our models are as follows: Across a wide range of Fdil, most models display positive correlations between [P/Fe], [N/Fe], [O/Fe], [Al/Fe]$, [Si/Fe], [S/Fe], and [Si/S]. The [Ce/Fe] ratios in P-rich stars can reach values up to 1 if the GMCs are additionally polluted by interacting low-mass asymptotic giant branch stars.P-rich star formation is highly unlikely in environments with a low interaction frequency between GMCs and ONe novae. P-rich stars exhibit anomalously low 14N/15N, 16O/17O, and 16O/18O isotopic ratios, offering a clear observational diagnostic to test this scenario. Assuming that P-rich Galactic field stars originate from GCs, we discuss the origin of their chemical abundance patterns. We suggest that the existence of P-rich stars provides direct evidence that GC-forming GMCs were polluted by pre-existing stellar populations.
item.dc:creator: Kenji Bekki, Takuji Tsujimoto

item.title: SEDust: A DUSTY-Based SED-Fitting Pipeline for Dust and Mass-Loss from AGB and LPV Stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.09086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present SEDust, an automated pipeline for spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting and the estimation of stellar mass-loss and dust-production rates. We apply this pipeline to quantify the mass-loss and dust injection rates in the dwarf galaxy NGC~6822, focusing on long-period variables (LPVs) and pulsating asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars as major contributors to dust feedback into the interstellar medium. The total stellar mass-loss rate is found to be $(3.70 \pm 1.16) \times 10^{-3}\ M_{\odot} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Two alternative methods (an LPV-based estimate and DESK) give totals that differ from this value by factors of $\sim$2.3 (lower) and $\sim$2.4 (higher), respectively, which we adopt as an estimate of the method-dependent systematic uncertainty. A positive correlation between stellar luminosity, intrinsic reddening caused by circumstellar dust self-extinction, and mass-loss rate is observed. The specific mass-return rate from AGB stars is $(7.40 \pm 2.30) \times 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, indicating that mass return from AGB stars alone is insufficient to sustain the current star formation rate of NGC~6822. This result implies the need for external gas accretion or additional mass-return mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Hamidreza Mahani, Narges Rostami, Atefeh Javadi, Hedieh Abdollahi, Jacco Th. van Loon, Francisca Kemper, Alvaro Sanchez-Monge

item.title: The N/O-O/H relation across large-scale environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.09330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The large-scale structure (LSS) of the Universe shapes galaxy evolution through its intricate web-like morphology, yet its specific influence on gas-phase chemical abundances remains uncertain. Particularly, a homogeneous comparison of the N/O$-$O/H relation, a tracer of the mass assembly and baryonic cycle, across distinct LSS environments has been lacking. In this study, we analyse a local SDSS galaxy sample curated within the framework of the CAVITY project -- dedicated to studying void galaxies -- in which galaxies are classified by their LSS environment into three groups: clusters, voids, and non-cluster/non-void (NCNV). We extract spectroscopic emission line fluxes from the central SDSS spectra and analyse how different galaxy properties affect the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation. For that, we subtract the main N/O$-$O/H relation from the data and study the dependence of the resulting residuals ($\xi_\text{N/O}$) on a set of parameters, including stellar mass ($M_\star$), $g-r$ colour, and star formation rate (SFR). We find that $M_\star-$related variables are the best predictors of the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation, with little influence of the recent star formation history. Regarding the LSS comparison, no significant differences are found for void and NCNV galaxies. Cluster galaxies, however, present a N/O$-$O/H relation systematically lower (with $\xi_\text{N/O} \sim -0.02$). Consistent with this shift and with $M_\star$ as a good predictor of N/O$-$O/H deviations, we find that environmental dependences are also reflected in fundamental scaling relations: both the MZR and N/O$-M_\star$ relations are different for cluster galaxies. These combined results point to mechanisms in the dense intracluster medium (such as strangulation or re-accretion of metal-enriched gas) as the primary drivers of these chemical offsets for galaxies in cluster environments.

item.title: Where the red rise stops: JWST/MIRI reveals a near-infrared turnover in the Little Red Dot Abell2744-QSO1
item.description: arXiv:2611.09397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact sources with a blue rest-frame UV, a steep red optical continuum and, often, broad hydrogen lines. They have been interpreted as dense stellar systems, dust-reddened active galactic nuclei, or black holes embedded in dense, dust-poor gas, scenarios that are hard to tell apart in the rest-frame UV and optical. We present JWST/MIRI F770W and F1000W imaging of the triply lensed Abell2744-QSO1 at z=7.04, probing rest-frame 0.96 and 1.24um. QSO1 is unresolved, and its steep optical rise stops near rest-frame 1um. Up to 1.24um, a T~4450K blackbody, or a hotter one reddened by dust, describes the continuum, with no sign of the hot dust seen in most type-1 quasars. Our statistically preferred SED fits produce the red continuum with (3-4)x10^9 Msun of stars, over 100 times the dynamical limit on the host mass, and are therefore disfavoured. An accretion disc in a dense gas cocoon respects this limit but over-predicts the 1.24um flux by 5 sigma. Super-Eddington accretion models with a thermalising envelope reproduce the turnover, but only for a black hole ~2.5dex less massive than the dynamical estimate. For a dust-reddened accretion disc (A_V ~ 2 mag), dust at ~1200K can re-emit at most ~2 per cent of the absorbed luminosity, and most of it would have to emerge at ~70-600K, unless the dust covers only a small fraction of the sky. The dynamics favour an accretion-powered source, but our data cannot distinguish dust reddening from processing by dense gas. MIRI imaging at >18um could separate these scenarios.

item.title: Violent relaxation redux
item.description: arXiv:2611.09531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collisionless self-gravitating systems, such as merging galaxies, have long seemed an exception to the statistical-mechanical principle that chaotic many-body systems relax to maximum-entropy states: Lynden-Bell's statistical mechanics of their "violent relaxation," constrained by exact conservation of phase-space volume -- equivalently, of infinitely many collisionless "Casimir" invariants -- has appeared not to be a good description. We propose that violent relaxation does give rise to Lynden-Bell's maximum-entropy equilibria, but that both are underpinned by gravitational turbulence, in which large-scale gravitational fluctuations drive chaotic phase-space mixing of the particles' distribution function. We derive the universal small-scale (sub-Jeans) spectra of this turbulence and show that it leads to phase-space-volume conservation being broken on a timescale only logarithmically longer, in the particle number N, than the dynamical (violent-relaxation) time. This timescale separation lets the system relax "adiabatically" through a sequence of Lynden-Bell equilibria, each corresponding to instantaneous values of the Casimirs. At long times, it approaches an equilibrium close to its "ground state": a distribution whose Casimirs have adjusted so that the system's energy is now its minimum possible energy. Thus, the system's universal tendency is toward a minimum-energy, maximum-entropy state. We corroborate this picture with 1D N-body simulations and hypothesize that it can explain the universal equilibria of galaxies and dark-matter halos.

item.title: The AIDA-TNG project: Galactic bar pattern speeds in self-interacting dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.09852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cosmological simulations within the standard cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm systematically predict higher values of the dimensionless bar-speed parameter, $\boldsymbol{R} \equiv R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ (where $R_{\mathrm{cr}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ denote the corotation radius and the bar radius, respectively), than those inferred from observations of local galaxies, a discrepancy known as the fast-bar tension. Since bar slowdown is primarily driven by dynamical friction with the dark matter halo, bar dynamics is inherently sensitive to the properties of dark matter particles. We aim to determine whether dark matter self-interactions alleviate or exacerbate the fast-bar tension, and to identify the physical mechanism behind the differences in bar dynamics between CDM and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models. We use the $51.7\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ box of the AIDA-TNG cosmological simulations, run with three different dark matter models: standard CDM, and two SIMD models one with a constant cross-section model (SIDM1), and the other with a velocity-dependent model (vSIDM). We identify barred disk galaxies with stellar mass $M_* > 10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$ at redshifts $z=0.2,\,1.0,\,1.5,$ and $2.0$, and measure the bar fraction, bar strength, bar length, pattern speed $\Omega_{\mathrm{p}}$, and the ratio $\boldsymbol{R}=R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$. The pattern speeds in the SIDM1 and vSIDM models are generally lower than in CDM at nearly all redshifts probed in this study. The subsequent slowdown proceeds with nearly 10\% more effective in the SIDM models likely due to velocity-anisotropy. Consequently, at low redshift the mean value of $\boldsymbol{R}$ is significantly higher in the SIDM models, indicating that the fas-bar tension is further exacerbated in these scenarios.

item.title: Multi-phase Carbon Structure and Dynamics in NGC 6334: Insights from CO, [C I], and [C II]
item.description: arXiv:2611.09871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present high-angular and velocity resolution observations of the emission lines of [CII] at 158 micron, [CI] at 609 micron, and the 12CO and 13CO (J=3-2) transitions toward the central region of NGC 6334, providing a detailed multi-phase view of carbon in this massive star-forming complex. By combining morphology and spatial scales information, kinematics, line profiles, and line ratio analyses, we quantify the distribution and physical state of ionized and atomic carbon, and carbon in its molecular form in CO. [CII] emission is the most extended, permeates the mapped region and is dynamically complex, while 13CO is compact and quiescent, and 12CO and [CI] occupy intermediate regimes connecting dense regions to transitional diffuse layers. We interpret these emission distributions such that the brightest [CII] emission traces photodissociation regions (PDRs) close to the H II region bubbles located along the central filament, while the extended [CII] emission arises from the more diffuse warm gas, indicating either cloud formation or dispersal processes. Remarkably, the [CI] is more extended than the 13CO, but less than [CII] and may probe the gas velocity structure resulting from colliding flows or cloud-cloud collisions. Line ratios involving [CII], such as [CII]/[CI] or [CII]/CO are systematically high, revealing widespread diffuse emission and localized UV-illuminated surfaces. Line ratio analysis and K-means clustering of [CI]/13CO versus dust continuum (cold 870 micron and warm 70 micron) emission reveal stratified chemical structure that UV photons penetrate deeply into the clumpy ridge (Av~18), suggesting a porous PDR. These results together depict that NGC 6334 is a clumpy, feedback-dominated PDR ridge with coexisting carbon phases, where [CI] and [CII] also trace dynamical processing through multiple velocity components linked to cloud-cloud collisions.

item.title: SN 2026ahvu in NGC 1433 May Be a Prompt Type Ia Supernova with a Delay Time Under 100 Myr
item.description: arXiv:2611.09875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SN 2026ahvu is a Type Ia supernova (SN) that occurred in the nearby galaxy NGC 1433. Using archival Hubble and JWST imaging from the PHANGS survey, we show that the SN lies within 0.19$''$ and 0.26$''$ of two UV-bright star clusters. This $0.19/0.26''$ separation corresponds to $8/11$ pc ($17/24$ pc) at the reported distances of $9.1$ and $18.9$ Mpc, respectively. The probability of finding an unrelated Type Ia SN this close to a cataloged star cluster by chance is only $\sim$0.4 %. Thus, SN 2026ahvu is likely the first Type Ia SN that can be associated with relatively young star clusters in a nearby galaxy. From spectral energy distribution fitting using HST+JWST (or HST-only) data, we find that the clusters have age estimates of $37_{-5}^{+3}$ ($57_{-9}^{+14}$) Myr and $95_{-13}^{+15}$ ($88_{-12}^{+14}$) Myr. Association with either cluster would mean that SN 2026ahvu should be considered a prompt SN Ia and provide one of the most concrete measurements to date of a prompt Ia delay time. The median age of the younger star cluster is close to the minimum possible delay time for SN Ia progenitors. If the SN is indeed associated with the younger cluster, it would imply that Type Ia SNe can occur almost immediately after white dwarf formation. If the SN is associated with the older cluster, this discovery still presents the first example of a prompt Type Ia SN with delay time under 100 Myr.

item.title: Expanding the Volatile Abundance Inventory for High-Priority K-Dwarf JWST Exoplanet Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.08676v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There are exceedingly few chemical abundance measurements available in the literature for K dwarf stars, especially for those with T$_{eff} <$ 4700 K due to an incompatibility of traditional analyses with their molecular-line-ridden optical spectra. To address the need for K dwarf abundance constraints, we present an elemental ([C/H], [O/H]) and isotopic ($^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O) abundance analysis for six K dwarf exoplanet host stars: K2-141, NGTS-10, WASP-43, WASP-69, WASP-80, and HATS-72. Each system hosts an exoplanet targeted by JWST characterization efforts, making host star abundances especially critical as baseline references. Using MARCS model atmospheres, the TurboSpectrum spectral synthesis code, and near-infrared IGRINS spectra, we derive novel [C/H] and [O/H] abundance ratios for these high-priority K dwarf host stars. We further investigate prospects for determining $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C and $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratios using $^{13}$C$^{16}$O and $^{12}$C$^{18}$O lines from the 2.3 micron CO bandhead. The observed spectra are too noisy to measure $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratios for the sample, but we do find sub-solar $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios for five out of six targets. We also derive uniform gyrochronological ages for each host star to compare with galactic chemical evolution models and identify underlying abundance-age trends. NIR H+K band spectroscopy provides an alternative to optical, atomic line-derived carbon and oxygen abundances for cool dwarf stars. The growing catalog of precise host star elemental and isotopic abundances complements ongoing observations of their companions and provides a baseline for understanding their chemical composition, origin, and evolution.

item.title: Unlocking Pandora's Secrets: Probing the Thermodynamics of Abell 2744
item.description: arXiv:2611.08847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Abell 2744 (Pandora's Cluster) is a massive galaxy cluster undergoing multiple mergers, characterized by a highly disturbed X-ray morphology, elevated intracluster medium (ICM) temperatures, and several radio relics associated with merger driven shocks. We present NuSTAR observations of Abell 2744 aimed at mapping its thermodynamic structure and constraining the presence of inverse Compton (IC) scattering from relativistic electrons. We measure the temperature distribution across the cluster and identify a prominent shock front with a Mach number of $\mathcal{M} = 1.58^{+0.42}_{-0.30}$, aligning with the southeastern boundary of the radio halo. The global NuSTAR spectra are modeled with single- and two-temperature thermal components, as well as thermal plus power-law models to test for IC emission. The spectra are well described by purely thermal models with an average temperature of $kT \approx 11$ keV, and we find no significant evidence for non-thermal hard X-ray emission. We derive a 90\% confidence upper limit on the $20-80$ keV IC flux of $ F_{\rm nt} < 2.31 \times 10^{-12} erg~s^{-1}~cm^{-2}$. Combining this with 1.5 GHz diffuse radio measurements from the VLA, we estimate a lower limit on the average magnetic field strength of $B > 0.2 \ \rm{\mu G}$.

item.title: Tidal Braking Does Not Dominate Open-Cluster Slow Rotators
item.description: arXiv:2611.08925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extended main-sequence turn-offs (eMSTOs) observed in open clusters younger than $2~\mathrm{Gyr}$ are commonly attributed to a spread in stellar rotation rates. Tidal synchronization in close binary systems has been proposed as a possible mechanism for producing slowly rotating stars. To test this hypothesis, we measured the radial-velocity (RV) dispersions of slow-rotator samples associated with the eMSTOs of eight open clusters using ESO VLT/GIRAFFE and SALT/RSS spectroscopy. We extended the analysis to 40 open clusters using Gaia DR3 RV measurements. The observed cluster RV dispersions are generally substantially smaller than those predicted for binary populations dominated by close systems with orbital periods for which tidal synchronization is expected to be effective. In particular, all 40 clusters in the Gaia sample have RV dispersions below the prediction of the $P=10$ d binary-population model. These results suggest that close, tidally synchronized binaries are unlikely to be the dominant origin of slow-rotator populations in young and intermediate-age open clusters, although a contribution from undetected or wider binary systems cannot be excluded.

item.title: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
item.description: arXiv:2611.09039v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.

item.title: Suppression of water-ice UV photodesorption on cosmic dust analogs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) photodesorption regulates the partitioning of water between interstellar ice mantles and the gas phase, yet laboratory yields are generally measured on planar substrates rather than on surfaces representative of cosmic dust. We investigate how grain morphology affects UV photodesorption from thin H$_2$O ice films of 2-6 monolayers deposited on planar gold and olivine, soot nanoparticles, and olivine microparticles. Samples were irradiated at 12 and 60 K with a microwave-discharge hydrogen lamp, and ice depletion was monitored by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and reflection-absorption infrared spectroscopy. On planar gold, the photodesorption yield increases approximately linearly with ice coverage, from $\sim5\times10^{-4}$ to $\sim2\times10^{-3}$ molecule photon$^{-1}$ between 2 and 6 monolayers, consistent with increasing UV absorption in optically thin ice; planar olivine gives comparable yields. In contrast, photodesorption is suppressed on particulate olivine and, more strongly, on soot, where yields are up to a factor of $\sim40$ lower than on gold at 12 K. Both experimental techniques confirm the strong suppression of ice depletion on soot. These results show that UV photodesorption depends not only on ice coverage but also strongly on grain morphology. The pronounced suppression on soot may reflect heterogeneous ice growth and altered energy redistribution within nanoscale ice domains, implying that yields measured on planar substrates may substantially overestimate photodesorption from the thin ice mantles of cosmic dust.

item.title: Through Ups and Downs: the Transient Lensing Behaviour of SIDM halos undergoing Core Collapse
item.description: arXiv:2611.09546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes can become extremely dense following gravothermal core collapse, motivating their use as explanations for unusually concentrated gravitational lenses. Using an emulator calibrated on gravothermal fluid calculations, we investigate whether increasing central density necessarily strengthens lensing. We follow initially Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes through core formation and collapse deep into the short-mean-free-path regime, and compute finite-source magnifications, critical curves, and source-plane lensing cross sections for isolated spherical haloes with elastic, velocity-independent self-interactions, including external shear in selected calculations. Lensing strength evolves non-monotonically: it initially decreases during core formation, rises during early collapse, and generally declines at later stages despite continued growth of the central density. This decline accompanies the emergence of a dense inner core whose mass and radius decrease within a more extended, lower-density core. Time-averaged enhancement relative to NFW haloes depends on the lensing statistic, halo concentration, and interaction cross section. Generalized NFW haloes with central cusps $\rho \propto r^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma \geq 2$ always have larger lensing efficacies than core-collapsed SIDM haloes of equal mass and are therefore poor proxies, including in terms of the demographics (size and radial thickness) of arcs and Einstein rings. The core collapse stage at which SIDM haloes are optimal lenses coincides with the epoch at which the characteristic core surface density is close to critical, which typically occurs during the early stages of core collapse. These results demonstrate that central density alone is insufficient to characterize SIDM lensing and that its evolving mass distribution must be modelled explicitly.

item.title: SQUALO II: Probing Accretion Through CO Molecular Outflows in Massive Star-forming Clumps
item.description: arXiv:2611.09588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular outflows probe protostellar accretion and mass transfer from clump scales to forming stars. We present an ALMA study of CO (J=2-1) outflows toward 13 massive clumps from the SQUALO sample, spanning a broad evolutionary range and exhibiting clump-scale infall. We identify 51 high-velocity CO lobes associated with 31 outflow systems and derive their physical and dynamical properties assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium. Outflow inferred accretion rates are typically 10^{-5}-10^{-3} Msun/yr, consistent with active massive star formation. The maximum outflow velocity shows little dependence on candidate driving-core mass, indicating that it is not a reliable tracer of protostellar mass in clustered environments. Outflow momentum flux correlates positively with clump surface density, whereas accretion rate shows a tentative, statistically nonsignificant decrease with increasing virial parameter. Total outflow inferred accretion rate shows a tentative positive relation with clump-scale infall rate but remains systematically lower, suggesting that the detected outflows represent only part of the large-scale mass flux. The clump L/M ratio moderately anticorrelates with projected outflow length, although projection, observational limitations, and the embedded source population prevent a unique evolutionary interpretation. Together with the continuum derived fragmentation properties, our results show that compact cores embedded within infalling clumps drive the outflows. The tentative relation between clump-scale infall and protostellar accretion suggests a possible connection across these scales, although our observations do not directly trace mass transfer from filaments to individual protostars.

item.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.09720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane (FP) test of an intermediate-mass black hole is informative only when the compact radio emission, hard X-rays, accretion state, and host association refer to the same accretor. We used published VLA, VLBA, \textit{Chandra}, and \textit{HST} observations of a radio-selected dwarf-galaxy sample to determine when present nondetections are constraining and what observations are required for a stronger test. The VLBA follow-up reveals that compactness alone does not establish association with the target dwarf, while for the best nuclear candidates the radio component relevant to the FP has not yet been isolated on the intermediate physical scales between the VLA and VLBA measurements. We therefore recast the FP as a forward question: for an assumed black-hole mass, how likely is a given radio observation to detect the compact core? The calculation includes intrinsic FP scatter, X-ray uncertainties, the radio spectral index, the accretion state, and source size relative to the beam. The existing VLBA nondetections have low completeness across the adopted intermediate-mass range and do not provide useful black-hole mass upper limits. Meaningful tests require deeper resolution-matched radio imaging, recovery of intermediate-scale structure, and contemporaneous measurements of the intrinsic hard-X-ray component. Because the calculation returns a mass-dependent detection function for each source, the same framework can be applied to larger dwarf-galaxy samples to quantify survey completeness and build selection functions for population studies of low-mass black holes.

item.title: Correcting for the effects of the point spread function in intra-halo light measurements and application to deep Hyper Suprime-Cam data
item.description: arXiv:2505.24395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The intra-halo light (IHL) is the diffuse stellar component that surrounds galaxies, groups, and clusters. Its formation is linked to the hierarchical assembly of the system, making it a key tracer of galaxy evolution. However, the low surface brightness of the IHL makes it challenging to detect and distinguish from the point spread function (PSF) effect of the telescope. In this paper, we present an innovative technique that corrects for PSF-scattering effects in astronomical images. We use this method to provide a statistically robust estimation of the IHL in galaxy groups and clusters by fitting an exponential model to this component using an MCMC optimiser algorithm. To test our methodology, we build 5440 mock observations of Galaxy And Mass Assembly (GAMA) groups using data from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program Public Data Release 3 (HSC-SSP PDR3). Each mock contains an IHL component with a flux fraction ($f_{\mathrm{IHL}}$) ranging from 0.01 to 0.5. Our results demonstrate the importance of properly removing the PSF-scattered light, especially at lower $f_{\mathrm{IHL}}$. The IHL effective radius is overestimated by $\sim9.1$ and $\sim2$ at $f_{\mathrm{IHL}}=0.01$ and $0.5$, respectively, while the IHL flux requires correction for $f_{\mathrm{IHL}} < 0.4$, with an overestimate of $\sim84.4$ at $f_{\mathrm{IHL}} = 0.01$. After applying our PSF correction, the recovered flux and effective radius are much closer to their true values. inally, we apply our methodology to HSC-PDR3 UD real observations of the GAMA group G400138 in the $\textit{g,r}$ and $\textit{i}$-bands, finding median IHL fractions of: $f_{\mathrm{g,IHL}}$ $\sim$ 0.19$^{+0.09}_{-0.01}$, $f_{\mathrm{r,IHL}}$ $\sim$ 0.08$^{+0.06}_{-0.02}$, and $f_{\mathrm{i,IHL}}$ $\sim$ 0.06$^{+0.04}_{-0.02}$.

item.title: The Baryon Budget of Galaxies across the First Billion Years
item.description: arXiv:2603.00230v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a complete census of the baryons in early galaxies to investigate the phases in which gas and stars reside, their corresponding budgets, depletion times, and stellar return fraction as a function of redshift and stellar age. We use the ColdSIM hydrodynamical time-dependent non-equilibrium chemistry simulations and perform a detailed analysis of the cold, warm, hot, and stellar phases for both bound structures (galaxies/CGM) and the diffuse IGM. We investigate in depth the cold HI and H2 components, explicitly computed in our simulations, and their relations with host mass, SFR, metallicity and depletion times. We also provide observational insights and discuss the implications for stellar mass functions, PopIII star formation and changes in the IMF. We find that cosmic gas prior to reionisation is mostly cold, while at later epochs the warm phase becomes dominant due to enhanced star formation activity and increasing UV reionising radiation. Stellar return fractions at these times are ~0.15-0.20, a factor of two lower than the values usually adopted. Cold, warm, and hot gas masses as well as HI and H2 components show increasing trends with mass and SFR, while depletion times decrease down to 0.01-0.1 Gyr with a weak metallicity dependence. The resulting star formation efficiency remains at the level of a few per cent and gas-to-star fractions decline with mass, influenced by local feedback and environment. Our findings are consistent with ALMA, VLA and IRAM surveys at later epochs, including ALFALFA, xCOLDGASS, GASS, xGASS, EDGE-CALIFA, PHIBBS, and ASPECS. Gas phases are quantitatively related to the underlying stellar populations and can be used to infer unknown quantities. In the appendix we provide fit functions describing the trends of the stellar return fraction, the main sequence, phase mass relations, gas-to-star fractions and depletion times.

item.title: Estimation of the magnetic field strength from ALMA dust polarization in the protocluster G327.29
item.description: arXiv:2603.23747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic fields and turbulence may play crucial roles in the evolution of molecular clouds and ultimately in the formation of dense cores and stars. Despite being studied in many molecular clouds, the exact role of magnetic fields and turbulence in star formation is still poorly understood. We report the high-resolution plane of sky magnetic field (B_pos) morphology towards the high-mass star-forming region G327.29, obtained with the 12-metre configuration of the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) telescope. From our analysis, we obtain a complex B_pos morphology in which the magnetic field orientation is uniformly distributed across the entire range from -90 to +90 deg. The observed area is composed of one filament and one dense central clump, both of which harbour multiple dense cores. The total magnetic field strengths (Btot) in these regions are 1.7 \pm 0.8 and 3.6 \pm 1.5 mG at a number density (n) of 1.5 \pm 0.3 x 106 and 2.3 \pm 0.7 x 106 cm-3, derived using the Davi-Chandrasekhar-Fermi (DCF) angular dispersion function (ADF) method. The corresponding B_tot obtained using the Skalidi-Tassis (ST) method are 0.6 \pm 0.3 and 1.1 \pm 0.5 mG, approximately three times lower. The virial parameters ({\alpha}_vir) in these regions are 2.8 \pm 1.9 and 0.5 \pm 0.4, suggesting that the regions may be gravitationally bound or unbound after accounting the errors. The ratio of turbulent to magnetic energy (~0.17-0.34) indicates that the magnetic field is dynamically more important than turbulence. The relative influence of turbulence and magnetic fields on core dynamics appears to depend on how B_tot scales with gas density (\r{ho}) in the densest regions. In summary, this work, enabled by high-resolution ALMA observations, presents a comprehensive analysis of the relative roles of magnetic fields, turbulence, and gravity in regulating high-mass star formation in G327.29.

item.title: Spatially resolved optical and mid-infrared spectroscopy of SDSS1335+0728: implications for the origin of the Ansky event
item.description: arXiv:2607.00921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The galaxy SDSS1335+0728 brightened abruptly in December 2019 (the \textit{Ansky} event) and has since been confirmed as the host of extreme X-ray quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) of debated origin. We constrain the origin of its transient activity using spatially resolved VLT/MUSE and JWST MIRI/MRS spectroscopy to characterise the host galaxy and its nuclear accretion history. The stellar kinematics reveal two counter-rotating stellar components and kinematically cold gas ($\sigma_{\rm gas} \lesssim 60$~km~s$^{-1}$), consistent with a past minor merger. The host is dominated by old stars, with ongoing star formation confined to a ring at intermediate radii. Ionisation diagnostics reveal a three-zone structure: a central accretion-powered region, where high-ionisation coronal lines ([\ion{Ne}{VI}], [\ion{Ne}{V}], [\ion{O}{IV}]) are predominantly concentrated, a star-forming ring, and a LINER-like outer region. A Balmer-line light-echo analysis yields a minimum ionising luminosity $\log L_{\rm ion,min} \approx 40.5$~erg~s$^{-1}$ at projected distances beyond the reach of radiation from the \textit{Ansky} event, suggesting nuclear activity prior to 2019. Strong silicate emission at 9.7 and 18\,$\mu$m indicates directly illuminated dust viewed through a low effective mid-infrared (MIR) optical depth; its 9.7\,$\mu$m strength lies at the upper end of the active galactic nuclei (AGN) distribution, closer to that of MIR-selected tidal disruption events (TDEs). The data are consistent with pre-2019 accretion from either a low-luminosity AGN (LLAGN) or a long-lived TDE remnant disc. In both cases, \textit{Ansky} is a slow, faint transient in a $\sim\!10^6\,M_{\odot}$ black hole with ongoing accretion prior to December 2019, offering an alternative to the ``faded AGN'' interpretation proposed for some QPE hosts.

item.title: Set them free: extending RAMCOAL to model massive black hole triplets in hydrodynamical simulations of galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2607.04121v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) and the higher-order multiples produced by repeated galaxy mergers evolve through regimes that cosmological simulations cannot resolve. These regimes determine merger delays, spins, recoils, and host galaxies at coalescence. We extend the RAMCOAL subgrid model to follow massive black hole triplets within hydrodynamical galaxy simulations. In the original three-stage binary model, black holes evolve as sink particles, undergo dynamical friction, and form bound binaries that harden through stellar scattering, gas torques, circumbinary-disc coupling, and gravitational-wave emission. When a hierarchical triplet becomes chaotic, RAMCOAL samples a library of outcomes from direct N body experiments and follows the resulting mergers, exchanges, and ejections alongside the accretion and spin evolution of each black hole. Isolated-galaxy tests with different triplet geometries show that orbital configuration alone can change which pair merges and its coalescence time. For the first time, we follow an MBH triplet to coalescence within a hydrodynamical simulation of gas-rich galaxies, coupling triplet-driven mergers to host-galaxy evolution. Subgrid integration costs less than 1 ms of single-core time per MBH system and time step, independently of particle resolution. The resulting coalescence properties reflect the environment encountered during subgrid evolution. RAMCOAL thus provides a step towards merger catalogues linking gravitational-wave signatures to the galaxies in which the black holes evolve.

item.title: Gas-Phase Metallicity and Nitrogen Abundances in Low-Mass Galaxies Down to $M_\star\simeq10^{6.6}\,M_\odot$ at $z\simeq4.5$--$9.8$ from JWST Lensing Cluster Surveys
item.description: arXiv:2607.15515v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze 405 deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra of star-forming galaxies at $z=4.5$--$9.8$ from multiple JWST lensing-cluster surveys, including DREAMS, SPURS, GLIMPSE-D, UNCOVER, CANUCS, GLASS, and ERO, to study chemical enrichment in intrinsically faint, low-mass galaxies. The sample covers $M_{\rm UV}\simeq-12$ to $-22$ and reaches $M_\star\simeq10^{5.7}\,M_\odot$, with 50\% of the sources at $M_{\rm UV}>-17.5$ magnified by $\mu>3$. From individual spectra and mass-binned stacks, we derive the gas-phase metallicity together with nitrogen and carbon abundances using the rest-frame UV and optical lines. We derive new empirical strong-line metallicity calibrations using direct-method measurements from stellar-mass-binned stacks, reaching a representative stellar mass of $M_\star\simeq10^{6.6}\,M_\odot$. Applying these calibrations, we trace the $z\sim6$ mass--metallicity relation down to $M_\star\simeq10^{6.6}\,M_\odot$, where it reaches $12+\log({\rm O/H})\simeq7.2$. A two-parameter linear fit gives a slope of $\alpha=0.318\pm0.037$, only slightly steeper than the local low-mass slope and broadly consistent with hydrodynamical simulations. In the $M_\star\simeq10^{7.7}\,M_\odot$ stack, N/O from N\,{\sc iv}]\,$\lambda\lambda\,1483,1486$ exceeds that from [N\,{\sc ii}]\,$\lambda6583$ by $\simeq1.4$ dex. The UV--optical difference could indicate a localized, highly ionized N-rich component whose high N/O and subsolar C/O resemble nitrogen-rich globular-cluster populations with $M_\star\lesssim10^6\,M_\odot$. The combination of these abundance patterns and a He\,{\sc ii}\,\W4686/H$\beta$ ratio of $\simeq0.03$, well above BPASS predictions, suggests that WR stars may contribute both prompt CNO-cycle enrichment and hard ionizing radiation, with the inferred WR population potentially supplying enough nitrogen to account for the excess on globular-cluster scales.

item.title: ASKAP discovery of a pair of large radio bubbles: on the origin of odd radio circles
item.description: arXiv:2608.22835v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the serendipitous discovery of a large, low-surface-brightness radio bubble in 944 MHz continuum data from the ASKAP Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey. The structure, centred on the elliptical galaxy LEDA 217397 at a redshift of $z=0.040$, spans $\sim$8.4 arcmin, corresponding to a projected diameter of $\sim$399 kpc, and consists of two partly overlapping shells both with radii of $\sim$114 kpc. The integrated flux density of the bubble is $56.8\pm2.9$ mJy at 944 MHz, implying a rest-frame 1.4 GHz luminosity of $\sim$ $1.4\times10^{23}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Combining the EMU measurement with MWA GLEAM-X data at 88--185 MHz, we derive a steep integrated spectral index of $\alpha=-1.04\pm0.04$, and a two-frequency spectral-index map suggesting a possible exterior flattening. Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) fitting indicates a massive ($\log M_{\ast}/M\odot = 10.97\pm0.09$), quiescent (SFR=$0.025\pm0.083\,M\odot$ yr$^{-1}$) early-type host with no mid-infrared AGN signature and no overdense environment. We compare the bubble with odd radio circles (ORCs) and large radio shells, and discuss three scenarios for its origin: a starburst-driven wind, a merger-driven shock, and AGN jet-inflated bubbles. The starburst wind is disfavoured on energetic grounds ($\gtrsim$$10^{59}$ erg required versus $\sim$$10^{8}$ yr electron lifetimes), and neither a halo-scale merger shock nor a spherical nuclear blast wave can explain the unusually regular, double-shell geometry; a bipolar nuclear outburst -- a relic AGN jet episode, possibly triggered by a supermassive-black-hole merger -- provides the most natural explanation, with later shocks possibly re-energising the plasma. Deeper broad-band radio, polarimetric, spectroscopic and X-ray observations are needed to confirm its nature.

item.title: Rapid Growth of Intermediate-Mass Black Holes through Disk-induced Stellar Disruptions
item.description: arXiv:2609.03701v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dense nuclear star clusters provide unique environments for studying the dynamical interactions between stars and massive black holes. When an accretion disk is present, dissipative star--disk interactions can capture surrounding stars, drive their inward migration, and ultimately lead to disk-induced tidal disruption events\,(dTDEs). The long-term feeding rate from this process, however, cannot be inferred from single-orbit migration estimates alone, as it depends on the coupled evolution of disk capture, collisional relaxation, stellar depletion and replenishment, and physical mergers within the star cluster. In this work, we use high-performance direct $N$-body simulations combined with analytic prescriptions for star--disk interactions to follow this coupled evolution for intermediate-mass black holes\,(IMBHs) with accretion disks embedded in dense stellar clusters. The simulations track the formation of the stellar cusp, the capture of stars by repeated disk crossings, their subsequent orbital damping and migration, and their eventual consumption by the central IMBH. We find that dTDEs can sustain stellar mass supply rates of $\sim10^{-3}\,M_\odot \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which exceeds the Eddington-limited gas accretion rate for IMBHs with $M_\bullet<10^5\,M_\odot$. These results identify dTDEs as an efficient stellar feeding channel for IMBHs in gas-rich dense stellar systems. As one possible application, this mechanism may help transform $\sim10^3\,M_\odot$ IMBHs into more massive black-hole seeds, provided that compact stellar clusters and accretion disks persist for $>30$ Myr.

item.title: ALMA Chemical Evolution (ACE) survey: the dust content of subsolar metallicity galaxies at cosmic noon
item.description: arXiv:2609.21040v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dust plays a key role in galaxy evolution by influencing star formation and shaping the observed spectrum of galaxies. However, at $z\sim2$ (cosmic noon) our knowledge of the dust mass budget is limited to the most massive, metal-rich systems. Here, we probe the lower mass, subsolar metallicity regime by measuring the dust mass of 25 galaxies at $z\approx2.3$ from the ALMA Chemical Evolution (ACE) survey. The sample contains star-forming galaxies in the COSMOS field with robust strong-line metallicities down to $\sim 0.3Z_\odot$. Using the dust continuum detected at 873$\mu$m or 1.3mm we constrain the dust mass by assuming an optically thin single-temperature modified blackbody (MBB). The resulting masses of the detected galaxies have a median of $M_\mathrm{dust}=6.4\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, which is 4-9x larger than those of $z=0$ galaxies at matched metallicity and stellar mass, but more than 10x lower than IR-selected galaxies at $z\approx 2$. We find positive correlations between dust mass and stellar mass, metallicity, and star formation rate (SFR). In contrast, we find that the $M_\mathrm{dust}/M_\mathrm{stars}$ (DtS) ratio scatters around $10^{-2}$ but has no clear with metallicity unless we adopt a metallicity-dependent prescription for dust temperature. We also find a positive correlation between $M_\mathrm{dust}/\mathrm{SFR}$ and metallicity that suggests that dust buildup becomes more efficient at higher metallicities, likely due to the role of ISM grain growth or enhanced dust survival. We also recover the relation between DtS ratio and specific SFR (sSFR), without evidence of a turnover at high sSFR that would signal inefficient dust buildup. Finally, we measure a large molecular gas fraction among ACE CO(3-2)-detected galaxies ($M_\mathrm{mol}/M_\mathrm{stars}\gtrsim$1) that potentially explains both the sSFR and DtS excess over $z\approx0$ galaxies.

item.title: How bursty star formation shapes spectral diversity at high redshifts: breaking degeneracies in early galaxy formation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03790v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: JWST has revealed an unexpected abundance of z>10 galaxies and striking spectral diversity. Here, we model bursty star formation histories (SFHs) to explore how they shape this diversity and whether spectroscopy can discriminate between explanations for the UV luminosity function (UVLF) excess. We find strong burstiness ($\sigma_{UV}(M_h=10^{10}M_\odot)$~0.9 mag), increasing toward low halo masses, is required to reproduce the z~6 UVLF and observed fractions of galaxies in recent star formation upturns and downturns, traced by SFR$_3$/SFR$_{50}$. This burstiness naturally reproduces UVLFs and SFR upturn and downturn fractions over z~6-11. With increasing redshift, we predict galaxies in recent upturns (SFR$_3$/SFR$_{50}>5$) increasingly dominate the UVLF bright end, reflecting rising accretion rates and burstier low-mass halos. This results in higher median emission-line equivalent widths (EWs), bluer UV slopes and weaker Balmer breaks at fixed $M_{UV}$, while distributions of these properties broaden. We find the downturn fraction (SFR$_3$/SFR$_{50}<0.2$) is particularly sensitive to stochasticity: increasing towards faint $M_{UV}$ if burstiness increases in lower mass halos, and evolving with redshift only if stochasticity does. However, the model underpredicts the z~14 UVLF, so we explore two models which match the UVLF: increased burstiness and increased star formation efficiency. From z=10 to 14, at fixed $M_{UV}$, increased burstiness predicts the downturn fraction increases by ~2x and the weak-emitter fraction (H$\beta$ EW<50{\AA}) by ~1.5x. By contrast, the increased efficiency model predicts a constant downturn fraction and declining weak-emitter fraction. Overall, our results indicate burstiness is important for explaining spectral diversity and evolution at z~6-14, and that spectroscopic samples spanning a broad $M_{UV}$ range can establish its role in the z~14 UVLF excess.

item.title: Rotational Excitation of HC$_5$NH$^+$ by He: Collision Dynamics and Astrophysical Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.08197v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The protonated cyanopolyyne HC$_5$NH$^+$ is an interstellar molecular ion of astrochemical interest, and understanding its rotational excitation is essential for interpreting its emission in molecular clouds. In this work, we construct a two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) for the HC$_5$NH$^+$--He system using the CCSD(T)-F12B/cc-pVTZ-F12 method. Rotationally inelastic cross sections are calculated using the quantum close-coupling (CC) method, and the corresponding collisional rate coefficients are obtained by thermal averaging over a Maxwell--Boltzmann distribution. These rate coefficients are incorporated into a non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) radiative transfer model to investigate the excitation of HC$_5$NH$^+$ in the cold dark cloud TMC-1. A global $\chi^2$ minimization analysis of seven observed transitions yields best-fitting values of $n(\mathrm{H}_2)=1.63\times10^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$ and $N(\mathrm{HC}_5\mathrm{NH}^+)=5.09\times10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$, with a minimum reduced $\chi^2$ of 0.87. The modelled line intensities are in good agreement with the observations. This study provides the first-principles collisional data needed to model the rotational excitation of HC$_5$NH$^+$ and offers new constraints on its physical and spectroscopic properties in TMC-1.

item.title: Galaxy and Halo Root Systems: Fingerprints of Mass Assembly
item.description: arXiv:2503.21015v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss what we call halo or galaxy root systems, collections of particle pathlines that show the infall of matter from the initial uniform distribution into a collapsed structure. The matter clumps as it falls in; projected through time, it produces filamentary density enhancements analogous to tree roots and branches, or branching river networks. This relates to the larger-scale cosmic web, but is defined locally about one of its nodes: a physical, geometric version of a merger tree. We find dark-matter-halo root systems on average to exhibit more roots and root branches for the largest cluster haloes than for small haloes, indicating their more complicated assembly, even in dark matter without gas physics. Also, we find that high spin manifests as curvier roots, and that many have mass contributions that start far away from central, compact protohalo cores. Root systems also show sensitivity to anisotropic infall, which we see some evidence for in a simulation with rather low box size.

item.title: Universal Dark-matter Density Profiles of Cosmic Filaments
item.description: arXiv:2604.05033v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the radial dark-matter (DM) density profiles of cosmic filaments in the hydrodynamical simulation TNG50. The cosmic web is extracted from high-resolution density grids at redshifts $z =$ 0, 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 using the DisPerSE algorithm. We show that the filament spine locations returned directly by DisPerSE do not accurately reflect the true density ridges. To address this issue, we introduce a "shrinking-cylinder" re-centering algorithm, which significantly increases the inferred central densities and restores the inner power-law behavior of the profiles. When the radial coordinate is scaled by the virial radii of the terminal nodes, the filament density profiles exhibit a nearly universal form that depends only weakly on redshift, node mass, and filament length. This result suggests that cosmic filaments, much like dark-matter halos, obey a form of structural self-similarity once an appropriate characteristic scale is introduced. By repeating the measurement using only smoothly distributed, unbound DM particles, we find that the apparent central cusp of the full profile is primarily produced by low-mass halos embedded along the filament spines, while the smooth component develops a flat core within $R/R_{\rm vir}\lesssim0.1$. The redshift evolution of this smooth component further suggests a transition from predominantly smooth filamentary accretion at high redshift to increasingly clumpy accretion at late times. Finally, we show that the universal filament profile is accurately described by a generalized triple-power-law model.

item.title: TDCOSMO XXVI: Uniform lens modeling of eight doubly imaged quasars
item.description: arXiv:2604.24908v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present the first uniform gravitational lens modeling analysis of eight doubly imaged quasars from multi-band observations with the Hubble Space Telescope. Previous time-delay cosmography analyses by the TDCOSMO Collaboration have primarily relied on quadruply imaged quasars, while doubly imaged systems, despite being more abundant, remain underutilized due to their fewer geometric constraints. Using an open-source $\texttt{Lenstronomy}$ framework, we reconstruct the lensing systems with a pipeline tailored for doubles. Comparing our results to the literature, the modeled Einstein radii agree at an average of 1.5$\sigma$, which is expected given data and modeling heterogeneity, while modeled image separations differ from Gaia DR2 measurements with an r.m.s of only 3.6 mas. We find a strong correlation between Fermat potential precision and the surface brightness of the spatially extended host arcs, establishing that arc surface brightness is the primary driver of mass model precision in doubly imaged systems. To further quantify the information contributed by the lensed arcs, we performed a conjugate point analysis that uses only the quasar image positions to constrain the lens mass profiles. The resulting posteriors are substantially broader than those from full image modeling, and a strong anti-correlation between mass parameter hypervolume and arc magnitude additionally confirms that arc brightness determines the degree to which the lens mass profile can be constrained in doubles. A hierarchical cosmographic analysis incorporating time-delay measurements and stellar kinematics to infer $\text{H}_0$ will be presented in a subsequent publication. The uniform pipeline and arc surface brightness trends established here will significantly accelerate the construction of time-delay cosmography samples from the large lens populations expected from LSST, Roman, and Euclid.

item.title: Origin and evolution of NiI and FeI in the coma of the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS throughout its trajectory
item.description: arXiv:2605.07652v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present high-resolution UVES+VLT observations of neutral nickel and iron atoms in the coma of the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS taken after perihelion. Metal emission was strong shortly after perihelion and persisted at large heliocentric distances. At $r_h \sim 2$ au the total metal production rate was found to be at least an order of magnitude higher than that of typical Solar System comets. Post-perihelion production rates exhibit clear asymmetry compared to the pre-perihelion behavior: production rates are higher after perihelion and decline more gradually with $r_h$, with the difference being stronger for FeI. The NiI/FeI abundance ratio, initially anomalously high before perihelion, evolved toward values comparable to Solar System comets near 2 au, and shows a weaker $r_h$ dependence after perihelion. To interpret these results, we revisited and extended the carbonyl hypothesis in which FeI and NiI are produced by the rapid photodissociation of Fe(CO)$_5$ and Ni(CO)$_4$ vaporized from the nucleus. Models that include the direct sublimation of carbonyls reproduce the observed rates and the high NiI/FeI abundance ratio. The temperature profiles needed to reproduce the observations were found to be shallower than the equilibrium $T \propto r_h^{-1/2}$ relation. The full dataset could also be reproduced using the temperature profiles extracted from a thermal model of the nucleus, but only with significant empirical modifications to the model. In particular, a significant reduction in the active areas through the perihelion was required. An additional transient heat source ($T \sim$ 120 K) was also necessary. This heat source, possibly related to the amorphous-crystalline ice transition, could explain the early NiI excess before perihelion. Within the framework of this modified thermal model, carbonyl sublimation occurs below the surface of the nucleus.

item.title: Identifiability of $g$ mode Resonances in Eccentric Binary Neutron Stars with Multidetector Observations
item.description: arXiv:2606.11959v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: $g$ mode resonances in eccentric binary neutron star systems are potential probes of internal stratification, superfluidity, composition gradients, and the equation of state. Although such weak dynamical tidal signatures are unlikely to be resolved with current detector sensitivities, third generation observations may make them accessible, in which case identifying the weak resonant phase shift would provide information beyond the bulk adiabatic tidal deformability. We build a four class dataset in an eccentric harmonic framework, containing point particle, adiabatic tide, resonant $g$ mode, and pure noise samples, and use Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) detector data to test whether this weak resonant phase signature can be identified from noisy time domain strain. The ET, CE, and ET+CE deep learning models reach accuracies of $0.650$, $0.809$, and $0.875$, respectively. On the same simulated samples, the matched filtering method reaches lower accuracies of $0.534$, $0.703$, and $0.718$. This result arises from the fact that the resonant correction manifests as a weak phase morphology difference superimposed on the adiabatic tidal background, whereas matched filtering is sensitive only to the overall similarity. Hence, in the presence of weak phase differences, the neural network employed for the classification task is better able to learn these local phase and morphology features from the complete time domain strain segment. The results indicate that joint third generation observations improve the identifiability of weak internal mode phase information.
